title: Zingiber officinale essential oil mitigates psoriasis-like skin inflammation by modulating inflammatory and proliferative responses: in-silico, in-vitro, and in-vivo studies.
authors: Singh, Vipin Kumar; Sahoo, Debasish; Agrahari, Kirti; Bhogal, Inderjeet; Roy, Sudeep; Khan, Ammar; Mukhopadhyay, Pradipto; Chanda, Debabrata; Chanotiya, Chandan Singh; Pant, Yatish; Rai, Vineet Kumar; Yadav, Narayan Prasad
one_liner_zh: 研究姜精油抗银屑病作用，涉及小分子与炎症靶蛋白的对接模拟，但对象为小分子-蛋白而非蛋白质-DNA互作，方法虽含分子动力学但与TF-DNA结合机制无关。
abstract: Psoriasis, a chronic skin disease characterized as keratinocytes hyperproliferation and inflammation, remains a clinical challenge due to limitations of long-term synthetic drug therapy. Plant drugs can meet this limitation therefore, in this study, we investigated the anti-psoriatic potential of Zingiber officinale (ginger) essential oil (ZOEO) through in-silico, in-vitro, and in-vivo approaches. GC/GC-MS analysis was done to characterize the phytochemical profile of ZOEO and analysis identified alpha-zingiberene, beta-sesquiphellandrene, beta-bisabolene, camphene, and ar-curcumene as major phytoconstituents. In-silico molecular docking and dynamics simulations were conducted that showed strong binding affinities of these phytoconstituents toward psoriasis-related targets IL-23, IL-22, TNF-alpha, and NF-kappaB. For in-vitro study, qRT-PCR and ELISA were performed to quantify TNF-alpha, IL-6, IL-1beta, IL-17 A, and IL-23 levels; and immunofluorescence analysis was used to evaluate NF-kappaB translocation in LPS-induced inflammation in RAW 264.7 macrophages. The anti-proliferative effects were assessed via cell scratch assay, proliferation assays, and TNF-alpha-induced cytokine production such as IL-6, IL-17 A, IL-22, and IL-23 in HaCaT keratinocytes. Results showed that ZOEO significantly suppressed inflammatory mediators and keratinocyte proliferation. For Iin-vivo study, PASI scores, CosCam scores, qRT-PCR, ELISA, histopathology, and immunohistochemical analysis of specific markers (IL-23, IL-17, CCR6, and NF-kappaB) were performed to evaluate the effectiveness of topically applied ZOEO against IMQ-induced psoriasis-like skin inflammation in BALB/c mice. ZOEO significantly reduced psoriasis-like symptoms, decreased inflammatory cytokine levels (TNF-alpha, IL-6, IL-1beta, IL-17 A, and IL-23), and downregulated the IL-23-IL-17 A signalling axis. Acute dermal toxicity was assessed in CF rats and rabbits as per OECD guidelines and no signs of dermal toxicity were observed in both models. In conclusion, ZOEO exhibits significant anti-psoriatic activity through modulation of inflammatory and proliferative pathways and highlights the potential of ZOEO as a safe phytomedicine for the management of psoriasis.
abstract_zh: 银屑病（psoriasis）是一种以角质形成细胞过度增殖和炎症为特征的慢性皮肤病，由于长期合成药物治疗的局限性，其临床治疗仍面临挑战。植物药物可弥补这一不足，因此，在本研究中，我们通过计算机模拟（in-silico）、体外（in-vitro）和体内（in-vivo）方法探讨了姜（Zingiber officinale）精油（ZOEO）的抗银屑病潜力。采用GC/GC-MS分析表征ZOEO的植物化学特征，分析鉴定出α-姜烯（alpha-zingiberene）、β-倍半水芹烯（beta-sesquiphellandrene）、β-红没药烯（beta-bisabolene）、莰烯（camphene）和芳姜黄烯（ar-curcumene）为主要植物成分。计算机模拟分子对接和动力学模拟显示，这些植物成分与银屑病相关靶点IL-23、IL-22、TNF-alpha和NF-kappaB具有强结合亲和力。在体外研究中，采用qRT-PCR和ELISA定量TNF-alpha、IL-6、IL-1beta、IL-17 A和IL-23水平；并使用免疫荧光分析评估LPS诱导的RAW 264.7巨噬细胞炎症中NF-kappaB的转位。通过细胞划痕实验、增殖实验和TNF-alpha诱导的细胞因子（如IL-6、IL-17 A、IL-22和IL-23）产生评估抗增殖效应。结果表明，ZOEO显著抑制炎症介质和角质形成细胞增殖。在体内研究中，通过PASI评分、CosCam评分、qRT-PCR、ELISA、组织病理学和特定标志物（IL-23、IL-17、CCR6和NF-kappaB）的免疫组化分析，评估局部应用ZOEO对BALB/c小鼠IMQ诱导的银屑病样皮肤炎症的有效性。ZOEO显著减轻银屑病样症状，降低炎症细胞因子水平（TNF-alpha、IL-6、IL-1beta、IL-17 A和IL-23），并下调IL-23-IL-17 A信号轴。根据OECD指南在CF大鼠和兔中评估急性皮肤毒性，两种模型均未观察到皮肤毒性迹象。总之，ZOEO通过调节炎症和增殖途径表现出显著的抗银屑病活性，并凸显了ZOEO作为安全植物药物用于银屑病管理的潜力。
